final_message:
Implemented `tokenize`, `lookup`, `isTruthy` and `render`. All 10 tests pass with `npm test`.

- **`src/lexer.ts`**: splits the template into text, value (`{{ }}` and `{{{ }}}`), `#if`, `else` and `/if` tokens. Unterminated tags throw `unterminated tag`. Single braces and a lone `}}` stay as text.
- **`src/lookup.ts`**: `lookup` walks dotted paths using `Object.hasOwn`, so `constructor` and `__proto__` resolve to nothing. `isTruthy` uses JavaScript truthiness, with an empty array counted as false.
- **`src/render.ts`**: parses tokens into a tree of text, value and if nodes. This is where the `unclosed {{#if}}` and `unexpected {{else}}` / `{{/if}}` errors come from. Values go through the filters left to right, then `String()`, then `escapeHtml` unless the tag uses triple braces. Unknown filters throw when the tag is evaluated.

Things to know:

- `tsc` isn't installed and npm can't reach the registry, so I did not run a type check. The code is typed strictly, but that is unverified.
- `{{ items.length }}` returns the array length. `length` is an own property of arrays, so the README's "own properties" rule allows it. Say if you want it blocked.
- The README doesn't cover `{{#unless x}}` or `{{/foo}}`. These currently render as value tags, so they produce empty output rather than an error.
